title: Four building blocks. Four jobs.

title: Why we combine them.
kit: Prompt: this run. Project: this context. Skill: this method. Agent: all of them.
Prompt: says what to do on this run. Alone, it is gone when the chat ends.
Project instructions: keep the context and the template. Alone, they stay in one Project.
Skill: keeps the method: steps, rules, output. Alone, it has no files and no schedule.
The input and a schedule: the files to read, and the When.
Together: the same checked result, every run, without you.

A scheduled task is a saved prompt that Claude runs hourly, daily, on weekdays, weekly or on demand. Its prompt calls your skill, and the run reads the file stored in that skill.

title: Three tools, three strengths.
kit: Claude reads and writes. n8n and Power Automate connect systems.
At a time, or when you ask
On any event, or at a time
On a Microsoft 365 event, or at a time
n8n cloud or the firm's server
IT, or staff trained by IT

title: What Claude cannot do yet.
kit: Where Claude stops, an automation tool starts.
Event triggers: scheduled tasks start at a time or on demand, not when an email or a file arrives.
Exact, high-volume moves: copying thousands of rows the same way every time is a job for fixed steps.
Company controls: it runs on your account, without the retries, alerts and approval trail IT expects.
Every system: it reaches only the apps your firm allows it to connect to.
Same words every time: AI may word a result differently on each run, so you still check it.

title: When to switch.
kit: Use both: the automation tool moves the data, and Claude reads and writes inside the flow.
The trigger is an event: an email, a form, a new file, a system update.
One flow touches three or more systems.
It runs hundreds of times a day, or must give exactly the same output.
Many people rely on it, so IT must own it: logs, retries, alerts, access.
It needs a formal approval, with a record of who approved.
